To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured the cross sections of the natFe(n, n′γ) and 207Bi(n, n′)γ reactions.

1) the experimental cross-sections of the prompt γ-ray emission by 14.1-MeV neutrons on iron and bismut are obtained; 2) the theoretical cross-sections are obtained by the Hauser-Fesbach model; 3) the sensitivity of the theoretical cross-section to the level density parameter, the neutron width and the gamma width of the compound nucleus is investigated.
the differential cross sections of prompt γ-ray production by fast neutrons on iron and bismith were measured.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of prompt γ-ray production by fast neutrons on iron and bismith.
the prompt γ-ray production in the reactions of natFe(n,xγ) and 207Bi(n,xγ) at neutron energies of 14.5 MeV.
the study of the prompt γ-ray production by neutrons on iron and bismith.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prompt γ-ray spectroscopy is a very powerful and useful tool in the investigation of nuclear reactions with fast neutrons.
the experimental results are in reasonable agreement with the theoretical predictions.
the prompt γ-ray method can be used for determination of the (n, γ)-reaction cross-sections, but it should be applied with caution and with a proper theoretical background.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the experimental data on the prompt γ-ray production by 14.1-MeV neutrons on natFe and 209Bi are obtained for the first time.
the experimental data are in a good agreement with the calculations.
the measurements of prompt γ-yield are useful for the determination of the cross-section of the (n,γ) reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prompt γ-ray yield can be used for estimation of the (n, γ)-reactions cross sections in the energy range from 1 MeV to several tens of MeV.
the method is applicable and can be used to obtain cross sections of the (n, γ)-type reactions.
the cross sections of the (n, γ)-reactions on iron and bismith are comparable to those of (n, n’)-reactions.
